title: corpXiv preprint | github.com/corpXiv/corpXiv | 2026-01-24 A Market-Conduct-Safe, Evidence-Anchored Decision Packet for AI-Assisted P&C Underwriting Design principles for auditability, adverse-action ...
abstract:
Agentic AI in regulated P&C insurance is constrained less by
model capability than by the inability to produce durable decision
evidence. Underwriting decisions persist for years, and regulators,
courts, and customers routinely require carriers to demonstrate what
was known at decision time, which rules applied, where discretion was
exercised, and who held authority for exceptions. Current AI
deployments optimize prediction and workflow speed but fail to
preserve this decision state; debug traces and explainability
artifacts satisfy engineers, not auditors. This paper defines a
minimal decision-evidence construct and a decision-spine architecture
that binds models, rules, human intervention, and escalation pathways
into replayable, auditable records, illustrated through worked
underwriting examples. Underwriting AI will scale in regulated
insurance only when systems are designed to produce owned, defensible
decisions that survive time.
